subject: Discrete Mathematics
description: The course aims to develop an understanding of mathematical reasoning and problem-solving using discrete structures essential for computer science.
objectives: Use mathematically correct terminology and notation.
Construct correct direct and indirect proofs.
Use division into cases in a proof.
Apply logical reasoning to solve a variety of problems.
course_outcomes: For a given logic sentence express it in terms of predicates, quantifiers, and logical connectives.
For a given problem, derive the solution using deductive logic and prove the solution based on logical inference.
For a given mathematical problem, classify its algebraic structure.
Evaluate Boolean functions and simplify expressions using properties of Boolean algebra.
Develop the given problem as graph networks and solve with techniques of graph theory.

modules.title: Sets, Relation and Function
topics: Image of a Set, Sum and Product of Functions
Size of a Set, Finite and Infinite Sets

modules.title: Principles of Mathematical Induction
topics: Basic counting techniques - inclusion and exclusion

modules.title: Propositional Logic
topics: Some Terminology, Proof Methods and Strategies

modules.title: Algebraic Structures and Morphism
topics: Algebraic Structures with one Binary Operation
Free and Cyclic Monoids and Groups
Algebraic Structures with two Binary Operations

modules.title: Graphs and Trees
topics: Degree, Connectivity, Path, Cycle, Sub Graph
Coloring Vertices, Coloring Edges, List Coloring
Definition, Properties and Examples of Trees
Cut-Sets, Cut-Vertices, Independent Component and Articulation Points

suggested_books: Kenneth H. Rosen, Discrete Mathematics and its Applications, Tata McGraw-Hill
Susanna S. Epp, Discrete Mathematics with Applications, 4th Edition, Wadsworth Publishing Co. Inc.
reference_books: J. P. Tremblay and R. Manohar, Discrete Mathematical Structures with Applications to Computer Science, TMH
Norman L. Biggs, Discrete Mathematics, 2nd Edition, Oxford University Press
